valuesChangedSinceApproval.reviewedBy: Decision approved by the product owner on 2026-08-19 after the measurements were reproduced independently against the shipped engine. The VALUES were computed during F-003 by the design and colour-science reviews, NOT by the person who approved the palette on 2026-08-14.
valuesChangedSinceApproval.note: `status` stays `approved` because it is the gate switch and the values DO meet every gate — worst |APCA Lc| 46.5 against a floor of 45, worst CVD separation 63.1 against a floor of 60. This field exists so the file cannot claim, in the one place a machine reads, that a human signed off values which postdate the signature. Re-approval is owed. SUPERSEDES the 2026-08-15 / ADR-0044 entry: the light values it corrected still stand, and only the three dark status tokens moved.

description: Machine-readable design tokens. The `contrast` gate reads this file and is BLOCKING from the moment it exists (F-003). Token NAMES are shadcn/Base-UI compatible so the wider ecosystem's tooling stays usable as reference — that is compatibility, not adoption (ADR-0033). Values are ours. Thesis: soft chrome, unaltered colour — every radius is generous except the swatch, which is 0 forever.

notes.authority: `oklch` is the authoritative field. `srgb` is DERIVED from it by the engine and rewritten by `pnpm --filter @irodora/design-tokens generate` — never typed by hand, and a hand-edited value fails the contrast gate (ADR-0043).
notes.usage: Every colour token declares `usage`, because a contrast gate cannot pick a WCAG minimum without knowing whether it is looking at text, large text, a non-text component, or a surface. The default is the strictest, so an omission fails safe.
notes.surfaces: Four tonal steps lifted from one ground, Material-3 style, rather than five arbitrary greys. The neutral carries a trace of warmth (hue 70-85) because a cold slate casts on every sample beside it.
notes.chroma: The interface is near-achromatic by rule. Chroma above 0.01 in ANY token requires an entry in `exceptions` — every token, not only surface and text ones, so that the exception count is the real count (ADR-0044). The single accent appears only in focus rings and selection.
notes.foreground3: `foreground.3` FAILS AA against every surface at small sizes and is therefore restricted to decorative use and text >= 18.66px. Micro-labels use `foreground.2`. It is declared `usage: "largeText"`, checked at 3:1 against the surfaces that carry secondary text, and emitted under a TypeScript type that is not assignable where normal text is expected.

swatch.well.role: MANDATORY neutral ground beneath every colour sample. Its hardest requirement — that a sample of ANY colour keeps a perceptible edge against it — cannot be expressed as a pairing, because the other side is an arbitrary garment colour; that is the two-tone keyline on swatch.hairline, gamut-checked in F-068. It IS a checked pairing in one direction, since border.strong must reach 3:1 on it.

swatch.hairline.role: One half of the two-tone keyline beneath a colour sample. OPAQUE, deliberately: a single translucent line is invisible at its worst case — rgba(0,0,0,0.14) against a black sample measured 1.00, which is no edge at all — and two translucent halves composite over the SAME sample, so their difference compresses to 1.15 against white. VERIFIED: scanning the sRGB gamut at 0.05 steps, the better of the two tones reaches at least 3:1 against every possible sample (measured worst case 4.23), and the two tones differ from each other by ~18:1 whatever sits behind them.
swatch.hairline.uncheckedReason: No declared pairing can express this: the other side of the line is an arbitrary garment colour, so there is no second token to name. It is NOT unchecked — packages/design-tokens/test/swatch-edge.test.ts scans the gamut and asserts the worst case, and it carries the shipped single-line design as a decoy that must fail. F-068.

foreground.role: Primary text. Warm off-white, never pure white.

foreground.3.role: Decorative and large text only. NOT for micro-labels.

link.role: Link text. Deliberately IDENTICAL to `foreground` — the underline is the channel, not the colour.

border.role: Hairline. Translucent overlay, never a solid grey — depth reads as lift, not outline.
border.uncheckedReason: A decorative hairline beside tonal elevation. WCAG 1.4.11 applies to visual information REQUIRED to identify a component, and a card here is already identified by its surface tint — the line is reinforcement. Exempt by the standard, not by convenience.

backdrop.role: The scrim behind a dialog or bottom sheet. Heavier than light, because dimming a near-black page needs more of it to read as dimmed at all.
backdrop.uncheckedReason: A scrim dims; it does not identify. WCAG 1.4.11 governs visual information REQUIRED to identify a component, and the dialog above it is identified by its own surface tint and its elevation — the same argument `border` makes. Contrast between the scrim and what it covers is not a thing the standard asks for, and inventing a pairing for it would assert a requirement nobody has.

border.strong.role: The boundary of an OUTLINED control, where the border IS the boundary — so WCAG 1.4.11 applies to it directly and 3:1 is not optional. Opaque and mid-neutral, deliberately: the translucent version it replaces reached 1.17 against every surface in light theme and 1.56 at best in dark, which is a line you can see only because you know it is there. It does NOT sit on `inverse`: a filled control's boundary is its fill against the page, not a border, so listing inverse would demand one colour clear 3:1 against both a near-white and a near-black ground, which nothing can.

inverse.foreground.role: Text on inverse — and, since F-087, the text on a FILLED status surface, which is what HeroUI's --success/--warning/--danger-foreground resolve to. It clears 4.5:1 on all three fills in both themes, so no separate token was needed. But in DARK it lands at APCA Lc 49.6 and 51.0 on status.ok and status.warn — a WCAG pass below the Lc 60 body-text floor, reported by gate 9. Read that as the measurement agreeing with ADR-0044: status colour belongs on the words, not behind them, and a filled status surface is a pattern to avoid rather than one this pairing endorses.

ring.role: Focus ring and selection. The only chromatic token in the PERSISTENT chrome — the status tokens are chromatic too, but they appear only while a state is being reported.

chart.1.uncheckedReason: A data series is separated from its neighbours by lightness, marker shape and a direct label, not by contrast against a surface — the greyscale ramp exists precisely so hue is not the channel. The requirement is series-to-series separation inside a chart component, which is F-017 work and cannot be expressed as a token pairing.

statusPairing._note: Every status token MUST pair with an icon token AND a text label. Three channels, always. A status expressible only as colour cannot be constructed — the pairing is enforced here so it cannot be forgotten in a component. RENAMED from `status` in F-003: this object and the top-level approval field `status` were both spelled `status`, and JSON keeps only the last, so `"status": "approved"` never survived parsing and `gate.contrast.blockingWhenStatus` compared against an object.

cvdPairs._note: Semantic pairs that must remain distinguishable under simulated CVD at severity 1.0. Asserted by the `cvd` gate. The product's own interface is held to the standard it applies to outfits.

salience._note: The salience rank of the status tokens, measured as |APCA Lc| against each theme's own `background`. RECORDED, not inferred: a rank read back out of the values can never disagree with them, and the F-067 defect was precisely that no order had been stated. Asserted by gate 9 via checkSalience.
salience.metric: absolute APCA Lc against the theme's own `background` token, background passed first
salience.why: Error is the loudest state in both themes. Holding this rank ACROSS the two themes is the invariant that makes them one system — and it is a rank of CONTRAST, not of OKLCh lightness, because the two grounds have opposite polarity and L rank does not survive that flip (ADR-0053).

radius._note: Material-3-scaled and generous — that softness is where the warmth comes from. swatch is 0 and never changes: corner radius removes sampled area from exactly the region the eye uses to judge a flat colour, and the effect grows as the swatch shrinks.

spacing._note: Editorial rhythm: the larger steps carry more of the layout than in a typical dense UI. 間 (ma) is a design element. EVERY STEP IS A MULTIPLE OF `base`, and ADR-0074 is where that stopped being an aspiration: the scale carried a 14, which no padding, margin or gap anywhere in the product used, while 12 and 16 were used 24 times between them and were absent here. The larger steps — xl2 upward — are used nowhere yet and are KEPT, because they are rhythm for layouts not built rather than a rule the scale breaks. scripts/verify-spacing-scale.mjs reads this object; nothing repeats it. THE STEPS ARE NAMED, AND F-103 IS WHY: this was a positional array, so a component wrote `nativeSpacing[2]` and nothing in that expression named 12. ADR-0074 renumbered every index above 1, which was safe only because nothing read the scale — five components read it by the time F-103 ran, and a step inserted or removed would have changed what every index above it meant while every call site still compiled and every style prop still received a valid number. The names follow `radius`, which was a named record all along; that asymmetry was the root cause of F-095.

size._note: Apple's floor, applied on web too. Comfortable is also accessible.

families.sans: Geist, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI Variable Display', 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif
families.mono: 'Geist Mono', ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Code', 'SF Mono', Consolas, monospace
families.jp: 'Noto Sans JP', 'Hiragino Sans', 'Yu Gothic UI', 'Meiryo', sans-serif

lineHeight._note: Japanese needs more leading than Latin at the same size. A single line-height for both is a layout that was only ever checked in one language.

numeric._note: MANDATORY on every colour value, coordinate, score and delta. A professional scans these in a column; proportional figures make a ΔE table unreadable.

elevation._note: Tonal, never shadow. Surfaces lift by tint — which is what the swatch rule required anyway, because a shadow tints what it surrounds.

motion._note: Motion must NEVER alter a colour mid-transition — the intermediate frames are plausible, so a user reads a colour that never existed. Every duration collapses to 0 under prefers-reduced-motion.

exceptions.reason: The focus indicator must be findable at a glance, and a near-achromatic ring on a near-achromatic surface is not. Recorded rather than exempted by classification: the ceiling governs EVERY token, not only the ones whose usage happens to be `surface` or `text`, so that the exception count is the real count. See ADR-0044.

A semantic status colour cannot be near-achromatic and still read as success. The ceiling exists so the interface does not compete with the garment sample; a status indicator is the one place where the interface must assert itself, and it is always accompanied by an icon and a text label (statusPairing), so the chroma is a reinforcement rather than the channel.

As status.ok. Chroma is where this token buys its CVD separation, because lightness is already carrying contrast, salience rank and gamut headroom. The value is the output of the search recorded in ADR-0044, not a preference; the gate run in that ADR is the evidence.
As status.ok. Error carries the highest chroma in the system (0.14 dark, 0.16 light) because it is the one state that must survive being glanced at.

contrast._largeTextNote: The px floor that makes `usage: "largeText"` mean something. WCAG 2.2 defines large text as >= 18.66px, or >= 24px bold (14pt/18pt at 96dpi). It lived only in prose and doc comments until F-017, while the rendered small-text check and the Text component's types both depend on it — a number three things agree about by copying it is a number that will eventually disagree.

chromaCeiling._note: Above this, ANY token needs an entry in `exceptions` — the scope is every token, so a chromatic accent cannot escape the rule by being classified nonText. The interface is near-achromatic by rule so that the garment colour is the only chroma competing for the eye.
